content.intro: In this lesson, you will work through reading html with .html() with a focused jQuery example. The subtopics below preserve the supplied curriculum coverage and connect the API idea to a small browser interface.
content.why_it_matters: This topic is useful because it turns getting an element's html into a repeatable implementation choice. DOM manipulation changes document content. Use text setters for plain text, create elements with known attributes, and avoid inserting untrusted data as HTML.

common_mistakes: Assuming a selector matched an element without checking the collection length.
Confusing jQuery collections with native DOM elements or live properties with markup attributes.
Using .html() with untrusted data or assuming client-side validation enforces server rules.
Treating a demo snippet as production-ready without testing failure and accessibility states.
